units.title: Python on a Raspberry Pi
units.blurb: Reading code like the computer does, and turning sensor readings into decisions.

units.title: Programs That Run Forever
units.blurb: State machines and steady control loops.

units.title: C on a Microcontroller
units.blurb: Integer sizes, overflow and bit masks: the bugs that bite on small chips.

topics.title: Tracing Code by Hand
topics.short: Follow a program one line at a time, writing down every variable, to know what it will do.
topics.trouble: Students guess what the loop does instead of writing down each pass, and miss the last pass or the first.

topics.title: Decisions from Sensors
topics.short: if, elif and else turn readings into actions; the order of the tests matters.
topics.trouble: Students write tests in an order where an early, broad test hides a later, narrow one.

topics.title: State Machines
topics.short: A robot is always in one state; each input moves it along a rule to the next.
topics.trouble: Students write long chains of if statements that forget what the robot was already doing.

topics.title: Loop Timing
topics.short: A control loop runs at a steady rate: period = 1 / frequency, and all the work must fit inside it.
topics.trouble: Students mix up milliseconds and seconds, or forget that the work itself takes time.

topics.title: Integers, Overflow and Bit Masks
topics.short: An 8-bit unsigned number wraps from 255 to 0; masks set, clear and test single bits.
topics.trouble: Students expect 250 + 10 to be 260 in an 8-bit variable, or clear a bit with OR.
